messages:
carlos_acme: Hey team -- streaming responses from the API are frequently arriving in two parts: a tiny initial chunk (a token or two) then nothing for ~6-10s, then the rest comes when the client reconnects. Client sees partial JSON then a reconnect. Happening for customers behind Cloudflare + ALB.

sam_support: Sorry you're hitting this, can you paste the curl you used and any proxy chain? Also, does curl -N show the same behavior?

carlos_acme: repro curl below. Note -N still shows the same pattern. We tried with and without TLS termination at CF.
```
curl -v -N \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \ 
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-large"
```

Verbose shows initial small chunk then 10s silence, then a FIN on reconnect. No 5xx.

priya_sre: Two quick calls out: (1) Cloudflare sometimes coalesces small HTTP/2 frames and will buffer until either a threshold or idle flush; (2) ALB in front of our origin can apply idle timeouts and proxy buffering behavior depending on the protocol mode. Can you share the response headers (including Transfer-Encoding / Content-Length) when you get the initial chunk?

carlos_acme: header dump: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream
transfer-encoding: chunked
connection: keep-alive
cf-cache-status: BYPASS
server: redwood/edge
content-security-policy: default-src 'none'

[then small chunk arrives]
```

sam_support: Good, CF shows BYPASS so it's going to origin. Priya, can CF worker code create any buffering? I know some worker transforms will buffer until you call writer.close(); not sure when it flushes frames.

cf_worker_bot: Note: Cloudflare Workers that proxy streaming must use streaming responders and not buffer the response. If there is a transform or text replacement, Worker will accumulate.

priya_sre: That aligns. Common misconfig: Worker doing any synchronous text op or using Response.text() which forces buffering. Also CF's HTTP/2->HTTP/1 translation can coalesce small writes. Ask customer: Are they using a CF Worker or plain Gateway?

carlos_acme: They use a Worker to inject a CSRF cookie on a subset of routes. We disabled the cookie and the stream improved immediately for a minute, then the issue returned.

ellen_infra: Logging from our side shows origin wrote a 1.2KB chunk at T=0.2s then periodic tiny chunks. No connection resets. ALB logs show no 5xx and healthy 200s. The pattern looks like an intermediary is aggregating small frames until a window or timer fires.

mike_runtime: On the runtime side we recently pushed a change that batches flushes for small prefix tokens to reduce tail latency/costs. It does call flush() on the socket, but if the proxy converts to HTTP/2 frames, you can still see coalescing. Suggest two experiments: (A) disable our prefix coalescing in a canary for this route; (B) ensure the origin sets explicit chunk boundaries and sends an initial larger chunk (e.g., 4KB) to force immediate flush through proxies.

carlos_acme: Quick repro steps we ran (matches customer env):
1) Route via Cloudflare Worker that sets cookie (script sample below).
2) ALB (application) -> Nginx origin (terminates TLS) -> upstream app server (gunicorn + uvicorn stream handler).
3) curl -N to Worker endpoint, observe tiny chunk then silence.

Worker snippet we used originally: 
```
addEventListener('fetch', event => {
  let req = event.request;
  // inject cookie for some paths
  if (req.url.includes('/embed')) {
    let res = fetch(req);
    return event.respondWith(res);
  }
  return event.respondWith(fetch(req));
});
```

priya_sre: That snippet looks pass-through; but if in other routes you call res.text() or do await streamResponse, CF will buffer. Also confirm Cloudflare 'HTTP2 Priorities' and 'Increase response buffering' feature flags are off.

sam_support: For ALB config: can you check whether ALB has proxy protocol enabled and that idle timeout is set high (>= 60s)? Also ALB may buffer to enforce content-length if proxy is got it.

ellen_infra: ALB logs we pulled: all requests show ELBStatusCode 200, TargetStatusCode 200, RequestProcessingTime ~0.01, TargetProcessingTime ~0.00. IdleTimeout on ALB currently 60s. Nginx config has proxy_buffering on by default; upstream chunked responses should pass but some modules will aggregate.

mike_runtime: Proposed mitigation steps (ordered):
- On origin Nginx: set "proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on; tcp_nodelay on;"
- In Cloudflare: ensure Worker is not accessing body and that Transform Streams are used for passthrough. If Worker must modify response, make sure to pipe with readableStream.pipeTo(writer) to keep streaming.
- On ALB: try switching target type to NLB (TCP passthrough) for a test to see if behavior changes; or enable connection: keep-alive with longer idle timeout.

carlos_acme: We applied proxy_buffering off and changed Worker to use streaming passthrough. Immediate improvement: streaming now emits tokens continuously. Reconnect cases reduced. We still saw one spike where initial token arrived then 4s gap.

priya_sre: That 4s could be an intermediate TCP Nagle delay or HTTP/2 frame coalescing on the client side. Recommend also: ensure origin sends a leading keep-alive heartbeat every 1s when idle (tiny comment event) and set TCP_QUICKACK where possible.

sam_support: Sounds like we've got a working mitigation. Carlos, do you want us to open an incident with Cloudflare support to verify Worker behavior? We can also run a canary with our runtime rollback to confirm the batching change's role.

carlos_acme: Please open CF ticket; customer wants an RCA and possible credit if it was platform misconfiguration. Happy to run a canary with you. Thanks all. :pray: 

mike_runtime: I'll schedule a canary rollback on the route for tomorrow morning PST and post the results here. If we see the issue go away, we'll prioritize a patch to adjust default flush thresholds.

priya_sre: I'll file an internal ops playbook entry with the mitigation checklist (disable proxy_buffering, worker streaming tips, ALB->NLB test) so support can triage faster next time.

sam_support: Thanks team — marking for escalation: billing credit assessment + CF ticket. Carlos, we'll keep you posted. :white_check_mark:
